title: Removing embedded points lowers the support dimension of the kernel
statement: Let $X$ be a locally Noetherian scheme [pqf-def-locnoeth] and $\mathcal F$ a coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module [pqf-def-coherent]. Among coherent subsheaves $\mathcal K\subseteq\mathcal F$ whose support is nowhere dense in $\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal F)$ there is a maximal one. For $\mathcal F'=\mathcal F/\mathcal K$, one has $\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal F')=\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal F)$, $\mathcal F'$ has no embedded associated points, and there is a dense open $U\subseteq X$ such that $U\cap\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal F)$ is dense in $\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal F)$ and $\mathcal F'|_U\cong\mathcal F|_U$, and $\dim(\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal K))<\dim(\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal F))$ when the latter dimension is finite and positive.

proof.text: On an affine open $V=\operatorname{Spec}(A)$, write $\mathcal F|_V=\widetilde M$ with $A$ Noetherian and $M$ finite. Apply the affine removal lemma to obtain a maximal submodule $N\subseteq M$ with nowhere-dense support; its quotient has the same support, no embedded associated primes, and agrees with $M$ after localizing at an element lying in all embedded associated primes.

The localization lemma identifies the quotient constructed on every principal affine localization with the construction from the localized module. Thus the affine submodules are compatible on overlaps; the gluing statement produces a coherent subsheaf $\mathcal K\subseteq\mathcal F$ and the quotient sheaf $\mathcal F'=\mathcal F/\mathcal K$.

The affine conclusions localize and therefore glue: maximality is preserved, the quotient has the same support and no embedded associated points, and the complement of the closure of the embedded associated points is a dense open $U$ on which the quotient and the original sheaf agree. This is exactly the three assertions in the statement.

Dimension. Let $d=\dim\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal F)$ be finite and positive; if $\mathcal K=0$ there is nothing to show. Let $Z$ be an irreducible component of the closed set $\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal K)\subseteq\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal F)$; it lies in an irreducible component $W$ of $\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal F)$. Since $X$ is locally Noetherian, the irreducible components of $\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal F)$ are locally finite (an affine Noetherian open has finitely many, Tag 0052), so the union of the components other than $W$ is closed and misses the generic point of $W$; its complement in $W$ is a nonempty open subset of $\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal F)$. As $\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal K)$ is nowhere dense in $\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal F)$, $Z\neq W$, so $Z\subsetneq W$ and every chain of irreducible closed subsets of $Z$ extends by $W$: $\dim Z+1\le\dim W\le d$. Taking the supremum over the components $Z$ gives $\dim\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal K)\le d-1<d$. Finiteness of $d$ is used for the strict inequality; positivity covers $\mathcal K=0$ under any convention for $\dim\emptyset\le0$.
